content.text: Every value in a computer program has a type. Understanding how different types are represented in memory is crucial for writing memory-efficient applications.

Primitive types represent simple values stored directly in the executing program's stack frame. Examples include integers, booleans, and characters. Because they have a fixed memory footprint, allocation and access are extremely fast.

The Stack is used for static memory allocation and thread execution. It operates in a last-in, first-out (LIFO) pattern. The Heap is used for dynamic memory allocation where variables can be resized or persist across functions.
Warning: Accessing values on the heap is slower than the stack because pointers must be dereferenced, and garbage collection must eventually clean up the memory.
